title: Energy flow: sun to plant to animal
subject: Life science

sources.title: NGSS 5-PS3-1: Use models to describe that energy in animals' food (used for body repair, growth, motion, and to maintain body warmth) was once energy from the sun

note.text: Almost all the energy for life on Earth starts in the sun.
note.remember: Life's energy starts with the sun.

note.text: Sunlight carries energy from the sun to Earth.
The plant's roots grow down into the soil, where it gets water. The energy, though, comes from above.

steps.title: Plant
steps.instruction: Trace the plant's stem and two leaves.

note.text: Leaves capture the sun's light energy and store it in the sugar they make. The plant makes its own food.

steps.title: Rabbit
steps.instruction: Trace the rabbit's body, head, ears and tail.

note.text: A rabbit can't make its own food. It gets energy by eating plants.
Eating plants makes the rabbit a consumer. Plants, which make their own food, are producers.

steps.title: Energy flow
steps.instruction: Draw the arrows: sun to plant, then plant to rabbit.

note.text: Arrows show which way energy moves. The energy in the rabbit's food was once energy from the sun.
note.remember: Arrows point the way energy goes.

steps.title: Energy's path
items: The plant stores energy in food
The rabbit uses the energy to hop
steps.why: The sun's energy is stored in the plant's food. When the rabbit eats the plant, that energy moves into the rabbit.
steps.hint: Where does the energy come from first?

steps.title: Trace it back
steps.question: The rabbit uses energy to run, grow and stay warm. Where did that energy first come from?

options.feedback: Yes. The plant stored the sun's energy in its food, and the rabbit got it by eating the plant.
Soil gives plants water and nutrients, but the energy came from sunlight.
Animals can't make energy. The rabbit got it from the plant, and the plant from the sun.
Plants need water, but the energy in their food came from the sun.

steps.title: Extend
steps.instruction: Add a fox to the model.
steps.question: A fox eats the rabbit. Where did the fox's energy first come from?

options.text: The sun, passed on through the plant and the rabbit
options.feedback: Right. Even a meat-eater's energy started as sunlight, passed along from plant to rabbit to fox.
The rabbit passed it on, but the rabbit got it from the plant, and the plant from the sun.
The fox gets energy from food. Follow it back: rabbit, plant, sun.
Every animal needs energy, and a fox's comes, in the end, from the sun.
